developing and implementing tools for efficient processing of massive amounts of sequence data and for efficient data retrieval from the database.
developing and maintaining a data base system for DNA sequence information.
data management for the genome projects.

the amount of data submitted to DDBJ in 1999 exceeds the total amount in the preceding 9 years, and the amount of data publicised is also large.
the Japanese genome projects are now at the stage of producing and publicising large amounts of data.
the DDBJ is a reliable, efficient and useful data bank.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to handle and publicise the data efficiently.
the data processing and data retrieval tools have been improved and are now more efficient than before, and that the data bank is becoming more and more user friendly.
we have developed a system that can efficiently process and publicise massive amounts of data while maintaining the quality of the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a data bank should not be a mere data storage place, but a service centre that provides useful information to users.
a large-scale sequencing project can only be successful with a strong data bank.
the collaboration with data producers and the development of efficient tools for processing and retrieving data are essential for the smooth operation of data banks.
